thread:
maria: heads up — Ginkgo reported a p99 latency spike on their dedicated pool since yesterday evening. crop of customer requests all hitting +120ms on tail compared to baseline. Can folks take async on this? :eyes:
kevin: got it. do we have traces or p99 spans? link them if available. also which model and node type?
jena: I pulled the traces from the customer bundle and a couple quick flamegraphs. model: gpt-medium-16k quantized. affected nodes: rk1-gpu-4 (same pool). no obvious token-level regressions, but KV cache miss ratio jumped. attaching short notes.
oliver: KV cache miss ratio up — could be prefix caching break or routing change. any rolling deploys last night from routing or kernel-selector?
maria: not from us AFAIK. ops shows a deploy at 22:11 by ci/bot but it was a tiny config tweak. support_alan can you paste the customer's ingestion pattern?
support_alan: customer says bursty bursts around 21:30–23:00 with bunching of short chat completions. SLA note: they hit p99 error budget thresholds yesterday, want updates.
srebot: deploy-bot: Completed deploy 22:11 UTC — change: routing.weight.adjust (ci/batch) — author: ci/bot
kevin: ok next steps from my side: can someone run a lightweight benchmark that reproduces their burstiness? command I use: ```rt-bench --model gpt-medium-16k --concurrency 60 --seq 64 --duration 300 --burst-profile ginkgo.json``` share results here.
jena: started a snapshot run on a staging replica with the customer's burst profile. early numbers: p50 ~ 20ms, p95 ~ 45ms, p99 ~ 130ms (matches customer's numbers). I also pulled a perf top during the spikes — saw sched stalls and occasional memcpy spikes.
oliver: memcpy spikes + KV misses makes me suspect a change in kernel selection that avoids fused attention or changed memory path. can you dump the kernel selector logs? there's a flag: `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_selector` on worker.
maria: dumping selector logs now and uploading to the thread. also capture command for support to run on their side: ```curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood/gather-trace -d '{"session":"<id>","mode":"kv,selector,mem"}'```
jena: added a short log excerpt: ```[kernel-selector] chosen=matmul_v2 fallback=matmul_v1 reason=mem_estimate_high [kv-cache] miss_rate=0.37 (baseline 0.05)```
kevin: that matches. we should validate if mem estimator regression caused selector to pick non-fused kernels. jena, can you run a pinned-run forcing fused kernels to see impact? `RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=fused_attention rt-bench ...`
jena: running forced fused now. preliminary p99 drops to ~75ms with same load. logs show lower memcpy. will keep it running for 20m and post full numbers.
oliver: good repro. if forcing fused helps, rollback path: revert the selector change from deploy 22:11 or add a profiling guard to force fused for this model class until we fix estimator.
maria: I can schedule a targeted rollback window if required. support_alan — would customer accept short maintenance window?
support_alan: they prefer minimal disruption but will accept a 15m maintenance if it restores SLA. need exact ETA and owner.
maria: ok i'll own the rollback coordination if we decide. jena/kevin/oliver please post final forced-fused numbers and we'll decide. thanks all :thumbsup:
